rationale: Evaluating omission of required braking requires characterising both the need to brake and whether the corresponding braking response occurs. H-1, SG-1 and FR-7 establish that response as part of the phenomenon, rather than merely an evaluation mechanism. H-1's failure to stop in time and FR-7.1 also support characterising braking initiation timing. The scope includes obstacle detection as a triggering state without extending to detection algorithms, sensor processing or their latency.
determining_elements: The vehicle's need to brake establishes when a braking maneuver is required.
The collision-avoiding braking response directly corresponds to the action whose omission T seeks to prevent.
The declared road, speed, weather and pedestrian-crossing conditions match H-1's operational situation.
Whether and when braking is initiated after obstacle detection is supported by FR-7.1's detection-triggered braking obligation and H-1's time-critical collision scenario.
